subject: Franska 4
title: Society topic: l'environnement
sourceSummary: Vocabulary and comprehension exercises around the environmental debate in France and Francophone countries — climate policy, everyday environmental choices, and how to discuss the topic with nuanced language.

questions.opener: A central concept in every environmental debate.
questions.explanation: "Le réchauffement climatique" means global warming — the gradual rise in the Earth's temperature. "Réchauffer" means to warm up again.

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly expresses "We should reduce our consumption" in French?
questions.opener: "Devoir" in the conditional expresses a recommendation, like the English "should".
questions.explanation: "Devrions" (conditionnel of "devoir") corresponds to the English "should" — a recommendation rather than an absolute obligation. "Nous devons" (present tense) instead means "we must", a stronger statement.

questions.opener: Think about what "renouveler" means — to renew.
questions.explanation: "Les énergies renouvelables" means renewable energy (sun, wind, water), as opposed to "les énergies fossiles" (fossil fuels such as oil and coal).

questions.prompt: Which expression is used to OPEN an opinion on a societal issue in a nuanced, formal way?
questions.opener: One of these options is too casual for an opinion piece or an oral presentation at upper-secondary level.
choices: À mon avis, il conviendrait de...
questions.explanation: "À mon avis, il conviendrait de..." (in my opinion, it would be appropriate to...) is a formal, nuanced way to open an opinion — suitable for opinion pieces and oral presentations. The other options are too casual/slangy for that context.

questions.prompt:
Read the text: "En France, le tri des déchets est devenu une habitude quotidienne dans la plupart des foyers, mais certains estiment que les efforts individuels ne suffisent pas face à l'ampleur du défi climatique."

What is the text's main point?
questions.opener: The sentence has two parts joined by "mais" (but) — which part carries the most weight?
choices: Waste sorting is mandatory in France
Most French people don't sort their waste
Waste sorting is common, but some argue individual efforts aren't enough given the scale of the climate challenge
The climate issue has been solved thanks to waste sorting
questions.explanation: The text says that waste sorting ("le tri des déchets") is a common habit, but also raises a critical voice: individual efforts aren't enough to match the scale of the climate challenge ("l'ampleur du défi climatique").
"L'empreinte carbone" means the carbon footprint — a measure of how much greenhouse gas a person, company, or product causes.

questions.prompt: Write a short, nuanced opinion (2-3 sentences) in French on whether individual choices (e.g. flying less) matter for the climate, compared to political decisions. Use at least one expression to nuance the opinion (e.g. "certes... mais", "il est vrai que... cependant").
questions.opener: A nuanced opinion acknowledges the counterargument before presenting its own position.
questions.answer: Certes, les choix individuels comme prendre moins l'avion ont un impact réel. Cependant, à mon avis, ce sont surtout les décisions politiques et industrielles qui détermineront l'avenir du climat, car elles agissent à une échelle bien plus large.
steps: Start by acknowledging the counterargument with "certes" (admittedly/granted) — this signals that you're taking in both perspectives before arguing your own: "Certes, les choix individuels comme prendre moins l'avion ont un impact réel" (admittedly, individual choices such as flying less do have a real impact).

Then pivot to your own position with a contrasting expression like "cependant" (however): "Cependant, à mon avis, ce sont surtout les décisions politiques et industrielles qui détermineront l'avenir du climat."
Finish with an argument supporting your position: "car elles agissent à une échelle bien plus large" (because they operate on a much larger scale) — "car" (because/for) links cause and conclusion.
This structure (acknowledge counterargument → contrast → own position → justification) is an effective way to build nuanced arguments in French, both spoken and written.

questions.prompt: What vocabulary and expressions do you need to discuss environmental issues in French at a nuanced, upper-secondary level?
questions.opener: Nouns, verbs, and nuancing expressions to have ready.
questions.answer: Nouns: le réchauffement climatique (global warming), les énergies renouvelables (renewable energy), l'empreinte carbone (carbon footprint), le tri des déchets (waste sorting), le développement durable (sustainable development), la biodiversité (biodiversity). Verbs: réduire (to reduce), polluer (to pollute), préserver (to preserve), agir (to act). Nuancing expressions: certes... mais/cependant (admittedly... but/however), il est vrai que... néanmoins (it's true that... nevertheless), à mon avis / selon moi (in my opinion), il conviendrait de (it would be appropriate to), d'un côté... de l'autre (on one hand... on the other hand).
